items.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013
items.q: his youngest brother was killed in World War I, he was a soldier. He was an Austrian soldier and he was killed by the Russians on the Russian front.

ctx.x: Yeah. And I wonder, did some of your extended family, aunts, uncles, etcetera, not take advantage of the opportunity to get out at that time?

Most of my father’s — his sister, his youngest brother was killed in World War I, he was a soldier. He was an Austrian soldier and he was killed by the Russians on the Russian front. He had another brother and two sisters. And his mother, of course, after my grandfather had died, was still there. When the war broke out, World War I that is, my father went and got them all out of there because it was very near the Russian border, and they were afraid of the Russians. Because the Russians were noted for pogroms…
And you yourself had a — I guess after going to Denmark there was an underground system?
